extracted.intended_audience: general public; journalists and media-industry researchers; members or prospective members of Japanese newspapers and related organizations
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the Japan Newspaper Publishers & Editors Association (日本新聞協会), its activities, codes, history, membership rules, and policy positions affecting newspapers (ethics codes, sales rules, tax eligibility, AI use, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 新聞倫理綱領 (Newspaper Ethics Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: 新聞倫理綱領 — an ethics code promulgated by the association aimed at raising the ethical standards of newspapers, broadcasting and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association is responsible for establishing and promoting the Newspaper Ethics Code (alongside other codes). Historically instituted at the association's founding (1946) and later revised (new guidelines in 2000). The code functions as a standard for ethical behavior in news gathering and reporting and is one of the association's core activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 新聞販売綱領 (Newspaper Sales Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: 新聞販売綱領 — rules governing newspaper sales and distribution established by the association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the codes the association formulates to guide commercial and distribution practices for newspapers (e.g., relationships with vendors, subscription arrangements). The page notes these codes are part of the association's work to raise standards but does not give full text; they are referenced as part of the association's rulemaking and public guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 新聞広告倫理綱領 / 新聞広告倫理要綱 (Newspaper Advertising Ethics Code / Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: 新聞広告倫理綱領（新聞広告倫理要綱） — ethical guidelines for newspaper advertising established and periodically revised by the association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association established advertising ethics guidelines (initially in 1958, revised in 1976). These set expectations for acceptable advertising practices in papers and form part of the association's regulatory/self-regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: 取材と報道 (Rulebook for Reporting and Coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: 「取材と報道」 — a compiled rulebook (ルール集) the association consolidates and publicizes covering practices for newsgathering and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a rules collection the association produces and distributes to guide members on how to conduct reporting and coverage; used for public relations and internal guidance. No full text provided on the page, but the association is explicitly credited with compiling and publicizing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 編集権声明 (Statement on Editorial Rights / Editorial Independence)
rubrics_metrics.description: 編集権声明 — a declaration regarding editorial rights the association issued (first published in 1948).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes the association published the '編集権声明' in 1948, articulating principles around editorial authority/independence. This functions as a normative standard for member organizations' editorial autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 加盟基準：発行部数1万部以上 (Membership eligibility: >=10,000 circulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: 加盟にあたっては発行部数1万部以上という条件 — the association requires an average circulation of at least 10,000 copies for membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why many small regional papers are non-members (many have only several thousand copies circulation). Also notes membership can be at parent-company or per-paper level in some groups (so organizational membership practices vary). The page lists exceptions and examples where corporate structures affect membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: 軽減税率の新聞対象基準 (Eligibility for reduced consumption-tax rate for newspapers)
rubrics_metrics.description: 軽減税率の対象となる新聞は「週2回以上刊行され、定期購入される新聞」であり、定期購入とは新聞販売店との定期購読契約を指す（コンビニ等で販売される新聞は対象外）。
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: during the 2013–2019 debates on consumption-tax increases and reduced-rate implementation the association lobbied for newspapers to be included. The government agreed the target items would include '加工食品' and '週2回以上刊行され、定期購入される新聞', and the page explains the operational meaning: subscription delivery via sales outlets qualifies; single-copy kiosk or convenience-store sales do not. Historical timeline of lobbying and law enactment (tax rate changes, implementation dates) is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: 生成AIに関する著作権立場・利用承諾要請 (Position on generative AI use of articles / consent requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: 声明（2024年7月17日）: 検索連動型生成AIサービスによる記事の無断利用は著作権侵害に当たる可能性が高いとし、各報道機関の利用承諾を得るよう求める立場。
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The association publicly asked that search-linked generative-AI services obtain permission from news organizations before using their articles, asserting unauthorized use likely infringes copyright. This is a policy/usage standard for third parties (AI services) and guidance for member outlets regarding AI-based reuse of journalistic content.
